HatchPattern__Brickwork__Meta.Meta__Description: Brickwork in section or on plan - evenly spaced diagonal lines at 45 degrees, rising to the right. The British convention, and the one a planning officer reads without a key.
HatchPattern__Brickwork__Meta.Meta__WhyPaperUnits: Every length here is PAPER millimetres, like the dash patterns in Na__LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Config__.json, so the hatch measures the same on the sheet at 1:20 and at 1:100. Pattern scale adjusts from there.
HatchPattern__Brickwork__Meta.Meta__Spacing: Four lines to a 12 mm tile, so 2.12 mm between lines measured square to them (12 / 4 / root 2). Close enough to read as a tone at 1:50, open enough not to fill in at 1:100.
HatchPattern__Brickwork__Meta.Meta__WhySeams: The lines run to the tile's edges and meet their continuation in the next tile exactly. No line passes through a tile CORNER and none runs along an edge: a corner is shared by four tiles and an edge by two, and ink there would need drawing by all of them. Na__LeHatch__SeamCopies paints what a neighbouring tile pushes across a seam, so a line keeps its full width where it crosses, at any line weight.
HatchPattern__Brickwork__Meta.Meta__OtherWay: For diagonals falling to the right instead, set Pattern deg to 90.

HatchPattern__Brickwork__Identity.Identity__Description: How this pattern is named, found and grouped in the pattern lists.
HatchPattern__Brickwork__Identity.Identity__Note: The standard section hatch for brickwork: single diagonals at 45 degrees. Blockwork is the same hatch crossed.

HatchPattern__Brickwork__Tile.Tile__Description: The repeating cell, in paper millimetres.
HatchPattern__Brickwork__Tile.Tile__Note: Square, so the diagonals close on themselves: a line leaving the top edge re-enters at the same place on the bottom.

HatchPattern__Brickwork__Defaults.Defaults__Description: What the pattern draws with until a use sets its own. The stroke is 0.25 pt (0.0882 mm) at scale 1 and grows with the pattern scale; a line weight typed in the panel does not. 'inherit' takes the colour of whatever carries the hatch - a vector's edge colour - until a pattern colour is picked.

HatchPattern__Brickwork__Glyphs.Glyphs__Description: Drawn about the glyph's own origin, y pointing DOWN, in tile millimetres. Strokes only: the PDF stamps a tile as lines and never fills one.

Diagonals.Glyph__Note: Eight pieces of four endless lines, x + y = 1.5, 4.5, 7.5 and 10.5 (and the same again one tile on). The nearest any comes to a corner is 1.06 mm.

HatchPattern__Brickwork__Placements.Place__Note: The whole tile is one glyph at the origin

HatchPattern__Brickwork__Bounds.Bounds__Description: How far a use may scale and turn this pattern before it stops reading as the material.
